coverage: Peninsular Spain, the Balearic and Canary Islands, Ceuta, Melilla and the minor North African territories, from the Instituto Geográfico Nacional outline published by geoBoundaries. Llívia takes its shape from the matching enclave in the French outline.
processing: Polygons are simplified to about 33 m north-south, with neighbouring units sharing edges; parent units are dissolved from the most detailed level. Spanish and Italian frontier edges within 3 km of the French outline are moved onto it and overlap is erased, so shared frontiers coincide. An outline edge is a land frontier when a point 100, 300 or 600 m beyond it lies inside a neighbouring country and a Natural Earth 1:10m land boundary line passes within 4 km. The Moroccan, Monégasque and Slovenian outlines include territorial waters, so edges facing them must also lie within 200 m of an OpenStreetMap land border way. Gaps of up to 3 km between frontier edges are closed unless they face open sea, and open pieces under 1 km are dropped. Neighbouring outlines (geoBoundaries) and the OpenStreetMap ways are used only for this test; none of their geometry is published. Each shared frontier is stored once (France holds its frontiers with Spain and Italy). Coastlines are not outlined. Mapped areas are spherical polygon areas.
